transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Jon (Redwood); Carlos, Anya, Jamal, Sofia (AtlasData)
Shared links: benchmark sheet https://redwood.app/sheets/atlas-poc | security pack https://redwood.app/sec/atlas

Summary: quick review of microburst TTFT improvements after kernel tweaks, streaming tail behavior, and next steps to validate KV prefix caching on staging. Discussed sequence-length distribution impact and a short debate about Dedicated vs Hosted for the production window.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — priya will walk through the kernel sweep results, then we'll look at streaming p95/p99 and discuss KV prefix caching experiment. any blockers before we start?
[00:18] Carlos (AtlasData): all good, thanks. we pushed last nights traces — you'd see the microburst case around the ecom-checkout flow.
[00:26] Priya (Redwood-SE): great, i pulled the logs, uh, and did a couple of runs on the 1.2B and 3B variants. initial note — TTFT improved on average from ~38ms to ~24ms with the new fused attention kernel on our bench A100 setup. that said, worst case spikes still at like 160ms for streaming handshake on 1:1 microburst events.
[00:48] Anya (AtlasData): tee tee eff tee? can you restate how you measure TTFT — is that server-side only or includes network?
[00:55] Priya: good call — that's server-side cold-path time-to-first-token, so excludes client network. we do have a second column for round-trip p50 which adds ~12-20ms depending on routing. sometimes the transcript had 'k v cash' in logs, sorry — it's KV cache.
[01:20] Liam (Redwood-AE): quick clarification, when you say fused attention kernel — that's the newer nv-llm style kernel we tested versus the legacy cuda kernels?
[01:28] Priya: yes, exactly. the fused kernel reduces memory copies and kernel launches. for shorter sequences (avg 256) batching works nicely and TTFT wins, but for long sequences (1k+) we see garbage collection and memory pressure, which slows streaming initial tokens.
[01:45] Jamal (AtlasData): right, our worst-case sequence length is 1,024 for the automated summarizer. typical is 220-300. those are the traces i uploaded. the microburst is when a user opens 8 tabs concurrently and we hit parallel inference.
[02:02] Priya: we simulated concurrency — with continuous batching there's a sweet spot. beyond ~40 concurrent streams per GPU, queuing pushes TTFT up. the solution paths: more aggressive early-exit batching, or smaller model shard per GPU and lower batch sizes.
[02:26] Carlos: can you explain the streaming tail? we saw p95 around 120ms but p99 at 420ms in our staging numbers.
[02:33] Priya: yeah p95 at 120ms is achievable after the kernel tune, p99 is where microbursts and context swap hit. p99 spikes are dominated by sequence-length variance and occasional model swap activity when we hit memory limit.
[02:50] Anya: does Redwood Dedicated help here or does it make little difference to microburst p99?
[02:55] Jon (Redwood-SRE): dedicated gives you predictable capacity and reduces noisy neighbor effects, but if the root cause is model memory pressure due to long sequences, you'll still see p99 spikes unless we apply KV-prefix caching and smarter routing. Dedicated plus prefix KV cache reduced p99 in our internal sim by ~30%.
[03:20] Sofia (AtlasData-Product): interesting, our SLO is 200ms p95 and 500ms p99 — are we within that after your changes?
[03:28] Priya: p95 yes (we're ~110-130ms), p99 borderline — with caching and minor infra changes we can bring it under 450ms. but we need the long-seq traces to validate.
[03:40] Liam: also worth noting the quantization profile — the q4_0 profile cut token throughput a little but reduced memory which helped long seqs. Priya, did you test q4_0 vs q8?
[03:50] Priya: i did a quick compare: q8 maintains fidelity but uses more memory; q4_0 drops memory usage ~28% which allowed an extra KV shard and reduced model swap frequency. quality was OK on Atlas's prompts but your team should validate against their eval set.
[04:07] Carlos: yeah we saw small hallucination uptick in q4_0 on some financial jargon prompts. that's a risk for us.
[04:14] Anya: are there hybrid options — like q8 for finance critical paths and q4_0 for lower-risk flows?
[04:20] Priya: yes you can route by intent — Redwood routing policy supports per-route model/quant selection. you could keep q8 for finance intents and q4_0 for notifications and fetches.
[04:30] Jamal: about KV prefix caching — what's the tradeoff on memory vs latency?
[04:34] Jon: KV prefix cache stores repeated prefixes in GPU memory, so you use more memory but reduce recompute and repeated attention, which lowers TTFT and streaming tail. the tradeoff is you can host fewer total models per GPU. our recommendation for Atlas during peak is to enable prefix cache only for the few hot routes.
[04:51] Priya: we have a small simulation in the sheet: enabling prefix cache for the checkout flow reduced p99 by ~35% in the 3B run, but dropped overall model density by ~18%.
[05:03] Maya: Sofia, does product have any flexibility on which routes are hot?
[05:08] Sofia: yes checkout and billing are top priority. other flows can be low-priority.
[05:12] Carlos: OK that helps. for the microburst case i care more about stability than squeezing every dollar out of model density.
[05:20] Priya: noted. next, quick dive into kernel sweep results — i have three kernel families: legacy cuda, fused-attn v1, and fused-attn v2 (new scheduling). on A100 bench, fused v1 gave 24ms TTFT median, fused v2 22ms, legacy 38ms. tail differences were smaller but fused v2 showed lower 95th.
[05:48] Anya: any correctness/regression tests? we can't accept changes that shift tokenization or outputs slightly.
[05:54] Priya: good call — we ran a smoke eval set and looked for token-shift regressions. v2 had one micro-token alignment issue on a very contrived prompt — flagged in the sheet. we can gate deploy with model-level canary and fallback policy.
[06:12] Liam: can we add an automatic rollback if nll or prompt fidelity drops beyond threshold?
[06:17] Priya: yes Redwood rollout supports regression alerts tied to eval sets. we can set up a canary with 2% traffic and a rollback if evaluation score drops more than X% — we'll propose thresholds.
[06:27] Jamal: what about memory alloc fragmentation — you mentioned garbage collection earlier. can we do pre-warm to avoid that on spikes?
[06:33] Jon: pre-warm helps. we can pin a fraction of GPU memory for stash and pre-allocate kernel workspaces. that reduces jitter but increases cost. it's a tradeoff.
[06:42] Carlos: price sensitivity — can you give rough delta for pre-warm + prefix cache vs baseline hosted? we need to justify it.
[06:48] Maya: i captured a quick cost delta in the pilot pricing doc — roughly 12-18% increase in infra cost to get p99 improvement and pre-warm; we can model it against revenue impact. i'll send the sheet after the call.
[07:00] Anya: how do we validate on staging? Jamal can we spin a 48h prefix-cache-enabled experiment with synthetic microbursts?
[07:07] Jamal: yes we can. i'll coordinate with priy a to flip flags. (laughter)
[07:12] Priya: ha — i'll set the exact config: kernel v2, prefix cache on checkout route, q4_0 for low-risk flows, q8 for finance. we'll run 24h with real traces replay and 24h with synthetic stress.
[07:25] Liam: also want to add a tracing hook to sample raw KV cache hits/misses per request so we can attribute p99 reductions to cache.
[07:33] Priya: good idea — we'll add that to logs and attach a short dashboard.
[07:38] Carlos: any legal/security asks?
[07:41] Maya: not new — you asked for SOC2 + SSO/SAML and KMS integration. we attached security pack link in the header; we'll also provide a brief compliance call if you want a deeper dive.
[07:52] Sofia: yes please, finance wants the KMS/HSM details before commit.
[07:55] Maya: noted — i'll schedule with our security lead.
[08:00] (brief crosstalk, someone drops audio)
[08:10] Priya: back to tuning: one more note on sequence length distribution — if your 1k sequences are rare (<2% of traffic) it's cheaper to route them to a dedicated small fleet that uses q8 and more memory rather than tuning the main fleet.
[08:26] Anya: interesting, route by length — can Redwood route by token-length header?
[08:30] Liam: yes, routing policy supports request metadata directives, including token_length and intent tags. we can send short flows to a low-latency fastpath, long flows to a high-memory pool.
[08:42] Carlos: what's the cutover complexity? we have existing clients that don't send token_length.
[08:46] Jon: we can compute token length at the edge and surface as metadata to the router — small CPU work but feasible.
[08:52] Jamal: timeline wise — if we run the 48h on staging early next week and we like results, can we do a canary in prod by the end of next week?
[08:59] Maya: conservative plan: 48h staging, 48h small canary (2-5% traffic) with rollback thresholds, then incremental ramp. that puts a full rollout earliest 2026-12-15.
[09:12] Sofia: okay, product is comfortable with that timeline if costs are shown.
[09:18] Priya: for instrumentation i'll add three dashboards: TTFT median, p95, p99; KV hit/miss; model-swap events. we'll attach links to the sheet.
[09:28] Anya: one more question — what about compiler/kernel selection differences across instance types? we test on A100 but our prod might be GpuX in cloud provider.
[09:36] Priya: good point — kernels are hardware-specific. we generate kernel config per hardware fingerprint; fused v2 needs newer CUDA and certain sm compute. we'll run a compatibility sweep and note any performance delta. i'll include a column in the sheet for target hardware.
[09:50] Carlos: ok please add GpuX results.
[09:53] Priya: will do.
[09:55] Liam: wrapping up, can we recap action items?
[10:00] Maya: sure recap — priya kernel sweep results and attach artifact; jon enable prefix cache on staging for 48h; carlos/an ya share long traces; maya send pricing and security pack and schedule security call. we also target a live kernel walkthrough on 2026-12-06.
[10:20] Carlos: confirmed.
[10:22] Anya: confirmed.
[10:24] Jamal: i'll set up the staging job and ping the team.
[10:28] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the sheet and calendar invites. bye.

End of transcript.
